_readme: Datos reales de la NASA usados en el juego. Cada hecho tiene su fuente (sources). Los eventos apuntan a un hecho con 'events' (id de evento -> id de hecho). Los flares reales estan en 'flares'; si existe data/donki_flares.json (generado con tools/fetch_donki.py desde la base de datos DONKI) se usa ese archivo en su lugar. Los hechos que ningun evento usa se conservan como reserva. Documentacion completa en docs/eventos_y_datos.md

rad.text: Curiosity measured about 0.67 mSv of radiation per day on Mars. Inside its spaceship it was 1.8 mSv per day.

iss_dose.text: Astronauts on the ISS get roughly 0.4 to 1.0 mSv of radiation every day.

gcr_cycle.text: The Sun's 11-year cycle changes how many cosmic rays reach Mars: they vary by a factor of two.

meda.text: Perseverance's MEDA sensors detected 374 dust devils in its first 365 sols (Mars days). The average one is about 29 m wide.

insight_rate.text: InSight data suggest 280 to 360 space rocks hit Mars every year and leave craters bigger than 8 m.

insight_dust.text: NASA's InSight lander ended its mission in December 2022 when dust covered its solar panels.

moxie.text: NASA's MOXIE made 122 grams of oxygen from Mars air in 16 runs. That is enough for a person to breathe for about 4 hours!

veggie.text: In 2015 ISS astronauts ate lettuce grown in NASA's Veggie box. It took 33 days to grow!

phoenix_ice.text: NASA's Phoenix lander found water ice only about 5 cm under the surface of Mars (2008).

phoenix_hard.text: Phoenix found rock-hard ice just a few inches under the Martian soil.

perchlorates.text: Phoenix found perchlorates, a type of salt that is not good to drink, in the soil of Mars (2008).

comms_delay.text: Radio messages between Earth and Mars take about 4 to 24 minutes to arrive, depending on where the two planets are.

mer_power.text: NASA's Opportunity rover made about 700 watt-hours of power a day from its solar panels, enough to light a 100-watt bulb for 7 hours.

kilopower.text: NASA's Kilopower test reactor ran at full power for 28 hours. Four Kilopower units could power a space outpost!

lava_tubes.text: NASA scientists say thick rock around ancient lava tunnels on Mars could shield explorers from radiation, space rocks and extreme temperatures.

donki_log.text: NASA's DONKI database records the daily space weather: solar flares, solar storms and more.

water_recycle.text: In 2023 NASA's space station recycled 98% of the water its crew used, including urine and sweat!

ice_cliffs.text: NASA's Mars orbiter found steep cliffs on Mars where thick sheets of water ice show. Some are more than 100 meters thick (2018).

dust_storm_2018.text: In 2018 a dust storm covered all of Mars. It blocked so much sunlight that NASA's solar-powered Opportunity rover went silent on June 10.

viking.text: NASA's Viking 1 landed on Mars in 1976 and kept working for about six years, much longer than the 90 days planned.

chile.text: In 2021 NASA astronauts grew Hatch chile peppers on the space station for the first time. They needed about four months to grow!
